title: Luxury Bathroom Suite Configurator
description: Users design a luxury bathroom suite by positioning a freestanding bathtub and an accent chair within a procedurally generated room. They adjust material finishes, wall colors, lighting warmth, and furniture placement while a real-time cost estimator and style-harmony score update based on their choices.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a luxury bathroom suite configurator. Generate a procedural room (5m x 4m x 3m) with a tiled floor using a repeating checkerboard pattern and four walls with configurable color. Load 'shared_assets/bath_day.glb' as the freestanding bathtub and 'shared_assets/SheenChair.glb' as a vanity accent chair. Center both models on the floor, bathtub near the back wall and chair near a side wall. Use GLTFLoader and auto-scale each model to fit proportionally in the room. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at eye-level (1.6m height), use OrbitControls with damping, constrain polar angle so the user cannot look below the floor. Lighting: one RectAreaLight simulating a ceiling panel, two warm SpotLights with shadows enabled, and a soft AmbientLight. Implement these interaction steps with parameter validation: (1) Click-to-select either furniture piece, highlight it with an emissive outline. (2) Drag selected furniture along the floor plane using raycasting, clamped within room bounds. (3) Rotate selected furniture with on-screen rotation slider (0-360 degrees, validated to numeric range). (4) A wall color picker (HTML input type=color) that updates all four wall MeshStandardMaterials in real time. (5) A lighting warmth slider (2700K-6500K) that adjusts SpotLight color temperature using a Kelvin-to-RGB conversion, validated to the numeric range. (6) A material finish dropdown (matte/satin/gloss) that changes the roughness and metalness of both furniture pieces with validated enum values. (7) Display a floating HTML overlay showing a calculated style-harmony score (0-100) based on contrast between wall color luminance and furniture finish, and a mock cost estimate that changes with finish selection. Validate all inputs before applying. Add a 'Reset Layout' button that animates furniture back to default positions using GSAP or manual lerp in the render loop. Render loop must call renderer.setAnimationLoop.
